project.title: Post-translationally modified and stop codon readthrough of recombinant Francisella tularensis Universal stress protein in Escherichia coli
project.projectDescription: Recombinant Francisella tularensis universal stress protein with a C-terminal histidine-tag (rUsp/His6) was expressed in Escherichia coli.  Endogenous F. tularensis Usp has a predicted molecular mass of 30 kDa, but rUsp/His6 had an apparent molecular weight of 33 kDa based on Western blot analyses.  To determine the source of the higher molecular weight for rUsp/His6, post translational modifications were examined.  Tryptic peptides of purified rUsp/His6 were subjected to liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) and fragmentation spectra were searched for acetylated lysines and polyaminated glutamines.  Of the 24 lysines in rUsp/His6, 10 were acetylated (K63, K68, K72, K129, K175, K201, K208, K212, K233, and K238) and three of the four glutamines had putrescine, spermidine and spermine adducts (Q55, Q60 and Q267).  The level of post-translational modification was substoichiometric, eliminating the possibility that these modifications were the sole contributor to the 3 kDa extra mass of rUsp/His6.  LC-MS/MS revealed that stop codon readthrough had occurred resulting in the unexpected addition of 20 extra amino acids at the C-terminus of rUsp/His6, after the histidine tag.  Further, the finding of polyaminated glutamines in rUsp/His6 indicated that E. coli is capable of transglutaminase activity.
project.sampleProcessingProtocol: F. tularensis rUsp/His6 with a C-terminus histidine tag was purified by Ni-NTA chromatography.  Samples were prepared either in solution or in gel slices, reduced with 10 mM dithiothreitol, alkylated with 50 mM iodoacetamide, digested with trypsin overnight at 37°C, and desalted on a C18 spin column.  Peptide separation was performed with a Thermo RSLC Ultimate 3000 ultra-high pressure liquid chromatography system using a Thermo Easy-Spray PepMap RSLC C18 column.  Eluted peptides were sprayed directly into a Thermo Orbitrap Fusion Lumos Tribrid mass spectrometer.  Data were collected using data dependent acquisition.  A survey full scan MS (from 350-1800 m/z) was acquired in the Orbitrap with a resolution of 120,000.  The 25 most intense ions were fragmented using high-energy collision induced dissociation with 35% normalized collision energy.   Fragment ions were detected in the Orbitrap with a mass resolution of 30,000 at 200 m/z.  Dynamic exclusion was set at 30 sec with a 10 ppm mass window.
project.dataProcessingProtocol: Data were subjected to database searching using Protein Prospector v 6.4.9.  Using a user protein database consisting of F. tularensis SCHU S4, digestion agent equal no enzyme, variable modifications of carbamidomethyl Cys and oxidized Met, and user defined modifications of acetyl lysine, putrescine Gln, spermine Gln and spermidine Gln.  Modified peptide candidates that were selected by Protein Prospector were checked by manual sequencing.
